newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria sells Stind glassmaker for $4 mln.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria sells Stind glassmaker for $4 mln.

text.p: Bulgaria's Privatisation Agency said on Monday it had sold 70 percent of Stind glassmaker to Cyprus-registered Glassinvest joint stock company for $4.05 million.
The buyer also pledged to repay 386.2 million levs of the Sofia-based glassmaker and invest $27.325 million in it over the next five years, the agency said in a statement.

Under the sale contract half of the price is to be paid in cash in up to 20 days after the contract goes in force and the other half should be paid either in cash or in Bulgarian government bonds in up to 50 days after that date.
According to the statement Glassinvest is a joint venture between Greece's Yioula and Frigorex companies and the Luxembourg-based Euromerchant Balkan Fund.

Euromerchant Balkan Fund is Global Finance's venture capital fund and its main aims have been to enter Bulgaria's investment market, to support the investment effort of Greek businesses and to become actively involved in the programme of mass privatisations planned by the government.
Yioula is the biggest glass producer in Greece and holds a 65 percent share of the country's market. Frigorex is the leading Greek producer of glass-door refrigerators, the statement said.
Bulgaria's Stind produces bottles and household glassware with 80 percent of output earmarked for export. Its turnover for the first nine months of 1996 totalled 1.008 billion levs.

Twenty percent of Stind's capital are to be offered to its personnel at preferential terms and the remaining 10 percent were set aside for repayment of restituition claims by former owners. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569
